body:
**Why.** `next_id` in cide-tasks mints `max(largest t-<n>, rev) + 1`, and `rev` bumps on every accepted mutation. So every comment, assignment or status change between two creates spends a number: terrastrike's board went t-772, t-774, t-776, t-780 (775 was the dispatch of t-774). The comment on `high_water_mark` admits to gaps only after a delete or an out-of-process merge, which understates it.

**Change.** Add `nextId` to `TaskFile` (`cide_ipc::tasks`): the number the next create takes, advanced only by a create (and by a repair re-mint), never lowered by a delete, `max` of both sides in `merge`. A file without it (every existing one) is settled once in `repair` under the old rule — past `rev` as well as every id, because ids deleted under the old rule are not in the file to be seen — and is contiguous from there. `validate` refuses a counter that is not past every numeric id.

**Checks.** `cargo test -p cide-tasks -p cide-headless -p cide-app`, `cargo test -p cide-ipc` then `cargo --locked xtask codegen`, `check:agents`, `check:agents-render`, `check:sidebar`, `check:commands`, fmt, clippy.

comments.text:
Done in the working tree (not committed).

- `cide_ipc::TaskFile` gains `nextId` (`#[serde(default)]`, default 1): the number the next create takes.
- `cide_tasks`: `high_water_mark`/`next_id` replaced by `largest_numeric_id`, `settle_next_id` (part of `repair`: a file with no counter is settled once under the old rule, `max(largest id, rev) + 1`; a counter behind the largest id is raised past it) and `mint_id` (finds the first free `t-<n>` from the counter and moves the counter past it). `create` and the repair re-mint both go through the counter. `merge` takes the higher side. `validate` refuses a counter that is not past every numeric id.
- Tests: `ids_are_contiguous_across_every_other_kind_of_mutation`, `a_file_without_a_counter_starts_past_its_rev_and_is_contiguous_from_there`, `a_counter_behind_the_largest_id_is_raised_past_it`, `a_counter_behind_a_live_id_is_refused_by_validate`, `the_merge_takes_the_higher_counter_from_either_side`; `an_id_is_never_reused_after_a_delete` and the re-mint test now assert exact ids.
- Journal entry "Task ids are contiguous (M61)"; doc references in `cmd/tasks.rs`, `cide-agents/tools.rs`.

Checks run: fmt, `cargo test -p cide-ipc -p cide-tasks -p cide-headless -p cide-app -p cide-agents`, `xtask codegen` (+ `--check`), clippy `-D warnings`, `tsc --noEmit`, `check:agents`, `check:agents-render`, `check:sidebar`, `check:commands`. All green. A copy of terrastrike's real tracker (93 tasks, rev 845) reads cleanly through the new headless binary; on first write it will settle to t-846 and be contiguous from there.
